nativeCanvasExecution.scope: Three successful 0.10.5 runs. The intermediate source-lens LED correction was followed by a successful rerun; the final rerun also clarified the historical cache note.

historicalIncidentAttribution.scope: The cache explanation inside nativeCanvas explicitly identifies the older interrupted preload; no current 0.10.5 Canvas assertion failure is claimed.

nativeCanvas.explanation: Real Canvas pixels rendered from the original simulation and PNG adapter. Rooms, equipment, actor positions and diagnostic camera magnification are explicit fixtures. Six effects originate from native shoot/hurtEnemy actions. Device completion (apart from the explicit embark fixture), sensor deployment/shutdown/depletion/recovery and attachment destruction use the original native actions after stated setup. This is neither a keyboard journey nor a full campaign completion.

decoder.preloadScheduling: Sequential categories through the production preload API; optional explicit garbage collection between categories when Node exposes it.

nativeImageCache.scope: QA harness only: a discarded image-selection pass records the exact paths for each frame, restoring Canvas pixels and all renderer properties. Native onload is awaited for those full-resolution images before the retained render; actual drawImage counts exclude selection passes. The production renderer and its normal browser image loading are unchanged.
nativeImageCache.reason: Historical 0.10.4 run: an initial all-resident preload was killed with exit 137 after 136 images and an observed 1165 MiB RSS. No assertion result or capture was claimed for that interrupted 0.10.4 attempt. This explains the retained bounded cache; it is not an incident from the present 0.10.5 run.
nativeImageCache.nativeReadiness: Native complete/dimensions can precede pixel readiness; every retained image draw waits for the actual native onload callback.
nativeImageCache.peakMeasurement: Maximum RSS sampled after each native PNG decode and isolated render; not a continuous process peak and not a performance comparison.

decoder.ancillaryMetadataExcludedInMemory: caBX provenance chunks only; the installed Skia decoder rejects these chunks. All source files and all IDAT compressed pixel chunks are retained byte-for-byte.

captureInventory.fileCountQualification: Fifteen capture paths for this edition; identical content may reuse historical Git blobs and is not claimed as fifteen newly unique pixel images.

findings: Armed walking sprites visually retain body identity, pistol placement and both facings. Rest/reduced-motion retain the previous static sprites.
Isolation source variant has complete flanges and stable world footprint; completion indicators remain inside existing screens.

Sensor indicator is now centered on the physical lens in active, pulse, remote-off and exhausted states. Pulse ellipse fits the diagnostic frame. Invisible RGB under alpha0 produces no halo in Canvas.
Rock breach apertures and boarding ramps preserve native surrounding walls, labels, native gate cues and final approach markers; foreground opacity is intentional native cutaway behavior.
Destroyed attachments retain their endpoints and world footprint while showing scorched inert resin.
Hive material stays in the two authored hive rooms and the clipped floor band; queen terrain retains native pixels.
limits: Isolated diagnostic fixtures and 50 explicit room setups; not a keyboard/browser journey or proof of complete campaign execution.
Generated project interpretations do not authenticate novel dimensions, likenesses or full 1:1 canonical fidelity.
The embark console completion is an explicit state fixture; ten other devices use native finishDevice after prepared work.

preparationIncidents.scope: The initial isolated distribution copy exhausted its temporary workspace volume. It was repeated on the larger local volume and verified successfully. This was a storage preparation incident, not a game-engine or Canvas failure.
Missing test dependencies were materialized from the exact parent blobs. No test expectation or protected release guard was altered to make the suites pass.

knownRenderingLimits.notClaimed: Cette injection ne décrit pas une panne rencontrée pendant le rendu Canvas normal.

publication.remoteCommitAndReadbackEvidence: The publication summary records the final commit and remote readback after this receipt is committed.

limits: Selected local suites and explicit full-resolution Canvas fixtures do not certify a keyboard/browser campaign, physical input testing or a complete animation cycle.
The 96 new cases contain 36 armed-gait presentations, 22 device states, five sensor states, six attachment states, 22 frontal-door states and five terrain cases.
Ten device completions use native finishDevice after prepared work. Embark completion is explicitly prepared as a state fixture.
The 50 rooms are explicit setups. Neither the 270 structured cases nor the loaded PNG count certify every campaign route or every novel omission.

The original module is sparse: 47 files were physically hashed and 2,983 entries compared through the unchanged Git index. The 125 historical archive entries were checked through the index, without physical extraction of the 59 deliverables.
The 924 MiB RSS figure is a sampled process maximum, not a continuous peak or a performance comparison.
The source-only record and captures are excluded from the playable overlay. The scoped copy is not a global production build.
Historical parent CI observations are separate from the local 0.10.5 evidence; no new-head CI success is asserted.
Generated likenesses, dimensions, materials and geography remain project interpretations; canonical global 1:1 fidelity and full-novel comparison are not certified.
The receipt intentionally omits its own digest from sourceFiles to avoid a circular hash. Its final text still requires the unchanged release text guard.
